# Tak-Dex Web V77.2 acceptance audit

## Checkpoint 1

- Verified clean V77.1-STABLE baseline `85e67e8b9eaef40bfa6d76cfbfa179d8bf50202c` against the GitHub main ref. Branch is `v77.2-development`.
- This checkpoint introduces the shared During/Final candidate application, selected-row scroll anchoring, offline status snapshot, and first pass on the shared presentation. The checkpoint commit is the commit introducing this entry.
- The final species remains at the existing slot root for compatibility. The explicit During species uses the existing `duringTargetId` field. Owned transitions still show Actual → active mode, while unowned explicit pairs show During and Final together. An inferred acquisition stage alone does not trigger a second artwork.
- The previous candidate handler wrote the selected species to Final even in During mode. The selector also constrained its options to descendants of the current acquisition start, which could hide a compatible earlier stage when the original path was a direct encounter.
- Previous offline views queried separate snapshots and could count the encounter index loaded in memory as a persisted download. The pack display now reads stored records and shares a snapshot with the dropdown and saved list.
- `node --check app.js`, `node --check sw.js`, and `git diff --check` passed. Browser baseline and candidate are served locally on ports 8812 and 8813.

## Evidence still required at this checkpoint

Targeted evolution and scroll flows, pack state transitions, browser regression runs, full screen inventory with rendered evidence, accessibility and scope review, and final draft PR/private preview verification.

## Verification and known limits

The full device, generation, game and team cross-product is not part of this browser audit. Samsung hardware, Android, physical pinch gestures and native JSON sharing are **Not tested**. Offline pack transitions used representative cache records plus the normal application removal workflow. Full remote download size and real interrupted-network behavior were not measured. The team recommendation badges report potential coverage, using verified route and learnset information where available. They do not assume that all possible moves fit into four simultaneous slots. Genuine acquisition unknowns remain visible.

Representative existing browser automation in `browser.cjs` under V77 still looks for the hidden During-game input directly. The candidate and unmodified V77.1 baseline both timed out at that obsolete entry point. The Round 12 editor test and V77.2 planner flow exercise the current UI. The four skipped Node tests are the optional external save-reference fixtures as identified in the test output.

## RC2 checkpoint

RC2 starts at RC1 `a3be2c0e96c73bee0b92f40a586f3d7b25c2c04e`. The commit introducing this entry implements the approved compact presentation on `v77.2-development`. The shell identifies itself as `V77.2 RC2` and uses `takdex-v77.2-rc.2`.

- Recommendations use the shared tinted-outline badges and a compact artwork, rank/name, types, Preview and BST header. Coverage and acquisition are independent disclosures. Coverage starts collapsed for a new context, and asynchronously enriched coverage replaces only the disclosure body. Ranking equations and inputs follow RC1.
- Planner artwork, names, badges, status and four move rows share content-sized tracks between adjacent cards. Stage context remains accessible without visible mode labels. Ownership, evolution paths, confirmation and slot scrolling keep the RC1 data model.
- Move acquisition uses separate display metadata derived from the existing timing evidence. The move compatibility engine retains its original text, rank and requirements. The same primary location still opens the map. The Move Checker captures the return position before resetting its panels, which fixes a 31 px return shift found with the compact planner.
- Move Checker By Type reuses the Pokédex filter row. Each tool retains its own options. The Offline Data manager keeps the persisted pack model and gives its legend a deliberate 2 × 2 layout.

Initial mobile evidence and focused regressions are saved under `/workspace/work/checks/v77.2-rc2`. The final acceptance entry records the completed runs, exact measurements and remaining limits.

## RC3 checkpoint

RC3 continues draft PR #4 from RC2 `51137c6004f5d8ed6c4e0c22901654354a54c859`. The commit introducing this checkpoint implements the requested planner, ranked card, Move Checker and shared control changes. The app reports `V77.2 RC3` with repository cache `takdex-v77.2-rc.3`.

The shared-weakness mismatch came from mixed rosters. The count used During/Final types and the existing defensive ability calculation, while the advice rebuilt its member list from raw final slots. The advice now consumes the same members that produced the count and retains their slot IDs for review actions. For example, Patrat and Eevee can share a Fighting weakness in During, while Patrat and Espeon do not in Final. The calculation and candidate ranking are unchanged.

Early verification rendered the supplied reference and working app at 360 and 412 px. The evidence and final results follow in the acceptance entry.

### RC3 acceptance results

The supplied HTML was served locally and rendered with Chromium at 360 and 412 CSS px. Side-by-side evidence uses the same viewport scale. The live app used existing game data and seeded teams. The reference's illustrative ranks, names and results were not copied into the app.

- 412 px [Planner and recommendation comparisons](rc3-evidence/412-comparison-1.jpg) · [Evolution, move and coverage comparisons](rc3-evidence/412-comparison-2.jpg)

| CSS px | Same planner fixture RC2 → RC3 | Flame Wheel/Hammer Arm row RC2 → RC3 | Approved reference → RC3 move result | Approved reference → RC3 short acquisition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 360 | 252.1 → 240.3 | 31.7 → 19.8 | 56.0 → 56.0 | 28 → 28 |
| 412 | 267.8 → 241.1 | 34.8 → 21.4 | 57.4 → 57.0 | 28 → 28 |
| 1280 | 237.6 → 237.6 | 22.0 → 22.0 | Mobile reference only. RC3 57.0 | RC3 28 |

Flame Wheel and Hammer Arm fit on one line at both mobile widths. The longer Fury Swipes → Flamethrower pair fit at 412 px and wrapped without clipping at 360 px. Its corresponding row measured 31.7 px on both adjacent cards at 360 px. The reference team example measured 239.7 px. The tested collapsed ranked card measured 141.6 px at 360 and 151.8 px at 412. The illustrative Starmie reference measured 158.8 and 173.8 px respectively. The live card keeps the accepted RC2 header density and natural path height inside the narrower existing editor.

Intentional visual differences include Tak-Dex's branded page background and fixed navigation, its existing touch-sized search and filter controls, and a separate compact Acquisition details row to preserve clickable source information alongside the native selector. Full selection options remain available to keyboard and touch users. Long names and real requirements can wrap, and the app preserves actual type, BST, acquisition alternatives, warnings, and stat data. Light theme uses dark badge text on the same tinted fill. The measured Normal badge contrast was 12.7:1 in Chromium light theme.
